title: Graduated renewal bands with dynamic usage floors and uplift guardrails
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Proposal for a renewal and expansion framework that replaces flat true-up mechanics with graduated usage bands, a dynamic usage floor, and explicit uplift guardrails. Goals: reduce churn from surprise bills, preserve predictable unit economics for Redwood, simplify enterprise negotiations, and codify how security questionnaire (SQ) related credits apply to renewals. Key components: 1) Usage bands: three graduated tiers (Buffer, Base, Surge) with defined uplift percentages that scale non-linearly; 2) Dynamic usage floor: anchor renewal baseline to the 6-month rolling median rather than last invoice to avoid over-crediting short spikes; 3) Grace buffer: customer-facing buffer equal to X% of renewal baseline that can be applied once in a contract year without true-up; 4) Multi-year smoothing: applied discount ladder that increases with commitment length but with a de-escalation clause tied to sustained usage drops; 5) SQ/CISO credit handling: standardized credit offsets for security questionnaire completion limited to X% of first-year ARR and staged over renewal years; 6) Operational controls: tooling changes required in Console to show projected true-up, visualize usage bands, and an automated renewal calculator for AEs. Trade-offs: complexity vs fairness (more rules reduce buyer friction but increase selling complexity), revenue timing vs retention (buffers lower short-term uplift but reduce churn), legal alignment (need clause for baseline recalculation). Deliverables: policy doc for sales, renewal calculator widget in Console, lawyer-approved contract language, rollout playbook for renewals team.
comments: 2026-03-05 Aisha Patel: Initial draft pulled from Q1 renewal feedback sessions. Core idea is to move away from hard true-ups to a banded model with a grace buffer. Added example anchors and proposed percentages (Buffer 0-10%: 0% uplift; Base 11-50%: 10% uplift; Surge 51%+: 25% uplift).

2026-03-08 Legal (reviewer: Dana K.) : High-level thumbs up but flagged that 'dynamic usage floor' needs tight definition and a right-to-audit clause. Requested sample contract language and an opt-in checkbox for customers preferring classic true-up. Assigned to PM to draft legal-ready wording.

2026-03-09 Solutions Eng (reviewer: Priya N.): Ran two renewal scenarios with existing customers. Observed that multi-year smoothing materially reduces churn risk for customers with volatile seasonal workloads. Suggested adding a minimum committed throughput requirement for multi-year discounts to avoid gaming.

2026-03-10 Data Science (reviewer: Mateo R.): Simulated 12 months of usage for 200 enterprise customers; projected ~12% decrease in one-time true-up revenue but a 4% increase in renewals retention over three years — net revenue neutral to positive. Will share dataset and Jupyter notebook link in attachments.
